name: toast
description: A temporary floating notification for system feedback — confirmations, errors, warnings, and async status. Built on Sonner (imperative API); dismissed automatically after a timeout or by the user.

intent.Default: Neutral informational message — no status implied.
intent.Error: Failed operation — pair with description naming what failed and what to do.
intent.Warning: Completed with caveats or attention needed soon.
intent.Loading: Async operation in progress — persists indefinitely, must be dismissed programmatically.

composition.structure: H AUTO-LAYOUT — icon-slot (16×16) → content (title + description, V AUTO-LAYOUT) → actions (action-btn + close-btn, H AUTO-LAYOUT)
composition.loadingVariant: action-btn is absent in Type=Loading — only close-btn is shown.
composition.iconNotes: Default has an empty FRAME (no icon); Success/Error/Warning use a 16×16 icon placeholder instance; Loading uses a spinner.

imperativeCalls.Loading: const id = toast.loading(message) — dismiss with toast.dismiss(id)

behavior.promisePattern: toast.promise(asyncFn, { loading, success, error }) — transitions Loading → Success/Error automatically.
behavior.toasterPlacement: Place <Toaster /> once in root layout — never inside a page or route component.

accessibility.liveRegion: aria-live=polite — messages announced without interrupting focus
keyboard: Alt + T to focus toaster region

constraints: Type=Loading must always have a dismiss path — pair with toast.promise() or call toast.dismiss(id) explicitly.
Use toasts for system events, not user decisions or form field errors.
Show at most one toast per user action — deduplicate at the call site.
action-btn is for a single immediately reversible action (Undo, Retry, View) — never for destructive confirmation.
duration: Infinity requires a close button or programmatic dismiss path.
Do not override action-btn or close-btn fills from the toast parent.
Place <Toaster> once in root layout only.

useCases: Confirming a settings save ('Settings saved.') immediately after the user clicks Save
Reporting the result of an async file upload — transitioning from Loading to Success or Error via toast.promise()
Notifying the user that a background sync completed or failed while they were working elsewhere on the page
Providing an Undo action after a soft-delete ('Contact removed' + Undo button)
Alerting the user to a session or quota warning that appeared while they were mid-task ('Storage 90% full.')
Confirming a copy-to-clipboard or share-link action that has no visible side effect ('Link copied.')

Default.whenToUse: Neutral confirmation with no status implication

Success.whenToUse: Operation completed successfully and the user should know

Error.whenToUse: Operation failed — user may need to act

Warning.whenToUse: Completed with caveats, or attention needed soon

Loading.whenToUse: Async operation in progress; duration unknown — always paired with toast.promise()

comparedTo.situation: A persistent message that stays on screen until the user acts (form error, expiry warning)
comparedTo.notInstead: toast (toast auto-dismisses and may be missed)

comparedTo.situation: The user must make a decision before continuing (confirm a destructive action)
comparedTo.notInstead: toast (toast is non-blocking and cannot capture a decision)

comparedTo.situation: A form field validation error that the user needs to fix before submitting
comparedTo.notInstead: toast (toasts are for system-level feedback, not per-field input errors)

comparedTo.situation: Feedback that must persist indefinitely (legal notice, critical outage banner)
comparedTo.notInstead: toast (even duration: Infinity toasts lack the persistent, in-context placement of an alert)

notes: Sonner imperative API — no JSX props at call site; <Toaster /> in root layout provides the portal.

changelog.change: Renamed sonner.tsx → toast.tsx for naming consistency with the design system component name.

darkMode.notes: No known dark mode differences — all tokens are semantic and mode-aware.

notes: File renamed from sonner.tsx to toast.tsx 2026-06-04. Internally uses the sonner npm package — that import stays unchanged.
